scope: Stage9 independent read-only design review of Controller Core construction and checkpoint candidate flow
recommendation: Extract construction first into a normal DungeonCoreFactory; keep save/plan atomic commit and host UI/clock replacement policy in Controller. Extract checkpoint candidate validation as a separate flow with an explicit final suspension boundary.

constructionBoundaries.contract: Player level HP/attack/stagger/poise and milestone growth precede departure customization; initial processing systems and conditional checkpoints/hasNextFloor/evaluation provider remain explicit.

Frozen departure preview intentionally constructs a temporary manager without processing bundle; captures into the temporary checkpoint store. Do not install as Runtime.Dungeon or add processing behavior.
Use route.Current.State and definitions.CreateCheckpointSession at the existing floor index; preserve restoration object, hasNextFloor and processing/database/provider bindings.
Use existing single restore API with identical processing bundle; keep candidate restoration separate from accepted runtime replacement.

flowRisks: A flow described as read-only must distinguish candidate construction/validation from manager.SuspendForCheckpoint(), which mutates the current model. Make that final ownership boundary explicit rather than hiding suspension inside a generic read method.

Keep TryRestoreMemoryCheckpoint Observe-before / finally Observe(false), ReleaseInput and QueueSnapshot in host so success, refusal and thrown IOException all exclude only read/initialization time and preserve existing debt.
Do not broadly catch restore exceptions or convert them into success/default definitions; existing integration tests distinguish returned error from thrown read errors.
Terminal checkpoint and non-Cleared receipt rejection must precede current model suspension and ReplaceManager. On failure preserve existing route, floor index, current model and save bytes.

NextDeparture activation writes missing run files before restoring and replacing old model; keep its existing write/read/runID/Terminal checks and atomic plan ordering outside an allegedly read-only candidate flow.
Do not adopt candidate Core into Runtime until existing ReplaceManager boundary; discarded preview/failed candidate must not suspend or overwrite active runtime.
Pass RNG/logger/factory source from the runtime; do not create new clocks, inputs or RNG on restoration or floor replacement.

Avoid one broad options object with implicit defaults that silently enables processing/evaluation in frozen-preview or return/blocked-start paths. Prefer named construction methods or explicit typed policy fields.
Keep legacy map/card combination resolution and definition hashes in host for this stage; do not normalize or recalculate old save contracts while moving constructors.
proposedResult: CheckpointCandidate with Manager, CheckpointSession and optional LoadedRoute; host updates route/floor fields and performs existing ReplaceManager order only after validation and current suspension succeeds.
regressionsRequired: Initial new run versus old save/return/blocked-start processing and provider policy
Frozen next-departure capture and no added processing behavior
Floor transition restoration and hasNextFloor boundary
Terminal/receipt rejection, read exception and failed current suspension preserve current state
Clock debt/input generations/queued commands across failed and successful restore
Runtime/Core identity replacement and no View-triggered recreation
limits: No source implementation, Unity calls or tests executed for Stage9 by this reviewer.
Factory extraction must preserve current constructor arguments and order; this design review does not introduce fixes to existing behavioral asymmetries.
